profile.headline: Former Software Engineer at Apple Inc.
profile.summary:
I remember first learning Final Cut Pro and feeling the magic of putting together videos and 3D animations. I had no idea that just a few years later, I would embark on a journey to help develop the next generation of video and motion graphics tools. I joined the Motion team at Apple in 2009 just in time to contribute to the first version of Final Cut Pro X. I moved from being a tool user to a tool creator, which is a powerful but scary jump for an artist to make. I thought I knew how to program--and then I met my team. They took me under their wing and I found mentorship, camaraderie, and friends (and a great coding style guide). Over the next fifteen years at Apple, I transformed a passion for 3D technologies and App building into a career, spending my time between the rendering team, and the UI team. I also fell down the color science rabbit hole, working on image correctness and color accuracy.

Parallel to my Apple journey, I started going to a computer graphics conference called SIGGRAPH; I first attended in 2006, and I fell in love with the community on the spot. I volunteered immediately to help run the conference the following year. Over the next fourteen years, I worked in the organization in various capacities: I've published and presented at SIGGRAPH, helped administrate different venues, adjudicated content in the general jury, and in 2013, I was selected to run the Emerging Technologies venue in full. A few years later in 2019, I helped co-found a new venue called Adaptive Technologies, to highlight principles of accessibility and adaptability in the conference at large. 

Recently, I've been taking up radio astronomy in my spare time. I've successfully been able to detect galactic neutral hydrogen radio signals and decode weather satellite images. My next project will be setting up an antenna to listen to the microwave radiation Jupiter emits. I've started a small amateur radio observatory in the San Bernardino National Forest, where I spend time living among the trees, stars, and radio waves.

I'm always excited to learn new technology stacks, and I'm enthusiastic about what the future holds. I've moved from OpenGL and GLSL to Metal, and I'm in the midsts of migrating my decades of experience with Objective-C into Swift and SwiftUI. For personal projects at home, I'll start a new NodeJS project and drop into pure HTML, CSS, and JavaScript--the only language that won't actively judge you as it throws errors.

positions.locationName: Los Angeles, California, United States · Hybrid

positions.title: Technical Editor for "OpenGL Programming Guide" 8th Edition (Red Book)
2011 Subcommittee for Art Gallery
positions.description: Produced trailer content and work with the Art Gallery team to exhibit the 2011 juried art works. Hosted artist talks and assisted the Chair in executing her artistic vision.

positions.title: 2010-2011 Session Chair
positions.description:
Chair a session of four talks on graphics, visualization, and 3D interaction technologies at SIGGRAPH. Responsible for introducing and  facilitating talks, with question and answer afterward.

Session Chair for the technical papers talk, "Speed of Light" in 2011.

positions.title: 2008-2010 Subcommittee for Emerging Technologies
positions.description: Work with the Emerging Technology committee  to produce the "E-tech" venue at ACM SIGGRAPH, including communication with contributors, contractors, and the General Jury.

positions.title: Administrative Support
positions.description: Work to coordinate contributors in the Emerging Technology venue at SIGGRAPH '08 and '09. I was tasked with handing equipment and material logistics, helping to run portions of the unified jury meeting, and budgeting for curated content. I was also the primary contact for contributors in organizing details leading up to the show dates.

positions.title: Graduate Researcher / Programmer
positions.description: Biological systems simulation and visualization, C++, OpenGL.

positions.title: Graduate Assistant Researcher
positions.description: Research in the areas of computer vision and low cost motion capture. Also afforded a lot of latitude in researching in areas of direct interest relating to my artwork, including embedded systems, hardware design, tangible interaction, and data visualization.

positions.title: Visiting Scientist
positions.description:
Worked on Emerging Technologies project for SIGGRAPH '07 and a research paper for the same year titled "Lighting-Aware Motion Capture Using Photosensing Markers and Multiplexed Illumination."

Worked on embedded hardware design, system integration, data visualization, and computer vision.

Paper Link: http://web.media.mit.edu/~raskar/LumiNetra/Paper/CONFIDENTIALraskarSig07OpticalMocapPaper.pdf

See more on Wikipedia:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_capture#Semi-passive_imperceptible_marker
